jobs.title: GIS Analyst, Bureau of Environmental Surveillance and Policy
jobs.description: The Bureau of Environmental Surveillance and Policy (BESP) in EH works to ground Health Department programs and policy in science and law to support a healthy and equitable natural, built, and occupational environment for all New Yorkers. We promote environmental health through legal and data-driven program support, using innovative methods to track environmental determinants of health with a focus on New Yorkers disproportionately impacted by environmental risk. We share data and research findings to encourage evidence-based decision making, and partner with communities in community science and outreach to address stakeholder concerns and empower residents.   The GIS Analyst supports field data collection for programs across the Division of Environmental Health including building and maintaining tools such as ESRI’s Survey123 and Field Maps for inspectional staff in the Bureau of Food Safety and other bureaus. Reporting to the Director of GIS in Environmental Health, the GIS Analyst trains field staff on these tools, reviews incoming field data for quality and accuracy, and works across the broader ArcGIS platform, including ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Pro, to support mapping and analysis needs. The GIS Analyst also uses Python and ArcPy to automate recurring GIS processes and improve the efficiency of data workflows. We aim to strengthen agencywide data capabilities by empowering our workforce, enhancing intra- and inter-agency data sharing, and using modern technology to yield trusted and integrated data and insights. A real-time and comprehensive view of city needs is needed to enhance public health actions and improve health outcomes for the most vulnerable New Yorkers. The CPHDS is working to strengthen citywide population health surveillance by better linking public health, healthcare, and social service data to fully characterize and improve the health of New Yorkers. PREFERRED SKILLS: • Four or more years of demonstrated leadership experience developing internally- and externally-facing data communication products like dashboards and web products. jobs.title: Healthy Aging Program Coordinator, Bureau of Equitable Health Systems
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity and Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. The Bureau of Equitable Health Systems (BEHS) is the health care systems bureau of DOHMH. Our mission is to apply policy, evidence, and practical expertise to improve equity in health care delivery at the individual, organizational and systems levels. The Health Care Access & Policy (HCAP) Office within BEHS drives policy, programming, and research that maximizes health insurance coverage and increases access to a fordable high quality, and coordinated primary care with a strong focus on health equity. HCAP has dedicated staff working to improve access to quality, culturally appropriate primary care for New Yorkers, particularly those who are at risk for poor health outcome, by ensuring that on-the ground programmatic work, policy, and data activities inform one another. Within HCAP sits the Healthy Aging Unit, a program that builds support for older adults and their caregivers and strengthens the NYC Health Department's ability to monitor and respond to the health needs of older adults. The unit offers an exciting, unique opportunity for a public health professional with an interest in disease prevention, healthcare policy, health insurance (Medicare/Medicaid), and research.   The Bureau of Equitable Health Systems seeks to hire a Healthy Aging Program Coordinator who must be able to effectively manage initiatives and multiple projects simultaneously in supporting the Bureau's mission.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Contribute to strategizing, developing, implementing, and evaluating program initiatives that help support the health of older adults and address intersectional inequities.  - Assist in research and quantitative data analysis on public health initiatives including health insurance and including reviewing relevant literature.  - Disseminate information and serve as liaison between the Healthy Aging Unit and other agency programs and assist with troubleshooting.  - Coordinate with other city agencies to align priorities related to Healthy Aging.  - Collaborate with policy-focused staff across the agency to analyze and interpret aging-related policies and policies related to health insurance for older adults.  - Coordinate communication efforts to internal and external partners.  - Prepare reports, as appropriate.  - Conduct background research and prepare proposals for new programs.  - Maintain up-to-date knowledge base on relevant policy issues including public health insurance programs, health reform and transformation initiatives impacting primary care and health insurance coverage and healthy aging.  - Assist in planning, coordinating, and evaluating educational events, community outreach activities, and Healthy Aging initiatives.  - Maintain and update Healthy Aging contact lists, partner networks, and program resources.  - Identify and coordinate community outreach opportunities and events to support NYC Health Department engagement with older adults. Initiate and support special projects as requested by unit leadership.  PREFERRED SKILLS: - Strong organizational and project management skills. - Outstanding interpersonal and writing skills. - Proficient in Microsoft applications. - Knowledge of primary care, Medicaid, Affordable Care Act and/or health care systems  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Infection Prevention & Antimicrobial Stewardship Specialist, Bureau of Communicable Diseases

jobs.title: Junior Bioinformatics Scientist, Bureau of the Public Health Laboratory
jobs.description: The Division of Disease Control's mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The NYC Public Health Laboratory (PHL) is one of the largest local public health laboratories in the United States where employees contribute to the health and safety of NYC residents by providing clinical and environmental laboratory testing services. PHL is committed to its mission to safeguard the health of all NYC residents by providing quality laboratory testing services that support the priorities of DOHMH and its community partners to prevent and respond to clinical and environmental public health concerns. The NYC Public Health Laboratory seeks a qualified City Research Scientist II to serve as a Junior Bioinformatics Scientist.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Assist with conducting bioinformatics analyses for sequencing data that support public health efforts Assist with developing or improving tools related to pathogen identification, outbreak tracking, mapping drug resistance determinants, variant analysis, genome annotation and phylogenetics, genomics data visualization. Assist with strengthening the application of genomic tools to support public health diagnostic testing for pathogens from clinical and environmental samples (e.g., wastewater). Conducting literature reviews and stay up to date with cutting edge scientific and epidemiological research and tools. Assist with mentoring and cross-training staff or research fellows at PHL. Collaborating with other team members and partners on genomics data management (e.g., SQL data bases, public repository uploads, other datasets). Participating in agency wide WGS journal club and genomic data exchange working groups. Developing tools (e.g., dashboards) or strategies (e.g., Docker-based pipelines) to improve accessibility of bioinformatics analyses to no bioinformaticians (e.g., epidemiologists, virologists, microbiologists). Drafting written protocols and maintain accurate records of software tools design. Writing original manuscripts for publication based on data analyses and product development. Maintaining quality assurance and control of HTS data generated by PHL to ensure reproducibility and accuracy of downstream bioinformatics analyses. This includes writing and designing SOPs and validation/verification protocols. Using best practices for code development, and documentation. Experience with common tools for Next Generation Sequencing Analysis (NGSA), including reference-based analysis and de novo sequencing analysis (knowledge of open source and commercial microbial NGS analysis pipelines) and genome annotation. Strong analytical and organizational skills; Excellent oral, inter-personal and written communication skills. jobs.title: Manager for Translational Epidemiology, World Trade Center Health Registry
jobs.description: The World Trade Center Health Registry (WTCHR) was created in 2002 to monitor and evaluate the physical and mental health impact on more than 71,000 persons exposed to the September 11, 2001 disaster. Housed within the Center for Population Health Data Science in a renowned and dynamic agency, WTCHR research influences national policies concerning healthcare for those who survived the attacks and contributes novel epidemiologic findings to the post-disaster public health literature. jobs.title: Naloxone Informatics Specialist, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use Prevention, Care, and Treatment (BADUPCT) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADUPCT develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  The Overdose Education and Naloxone Distribution Unit (OENDU) develops, implements, and evaluates initiatives to reduce and prevent opioid overdose deaths in New York City. The Unit provides naloxone, training, and technical assistance to over 350 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs) across New York City. OOPPs provide community-based overdose prevention, recognition, and response education and distribute naloxone directly to community members. OENDU solicits data from these OOPPs to evaluate their naloxone dispensing. DOHMH has its own OOPP and provides in-person and virtual overdose prevention training and naloxone via mail-based distribution. In addition, OENDU provides contract management, fiscal, technical, and programmatic support to at least 27 contracted OOPPs for strategic naloxone distribution and 4 contracted OOPPs for the implementation and management of 8 Public Health Vending Machines.   Position Summary:    The Naloxone Informatics Specialist will support the Overdose Prevention Unit by supporting the submission of accurate and timely naloxone distribution data, with the goal of preventing overdose deaths in New York City.  Under general direction from the Naloxone Data Coordinator, with wide latitude for independent judgment and initiative, the Naloxone Informatics Specialist will:  Job Duties and Responsibilities:    •	Collaborate with colleagues in OENDU and the Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) to gather and analyze data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution in NYC  •	Use Microsoft Access and/or R studio to clean and maintain data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC  •	Generate PowerBI dashboards and data tables to support the ongoing evaluation of naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC.  •	Solicit monthly naloxone distribution reports from over 190 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs); follow up with OOPPs who do not submit timely reports and provide technical assistance as needed  •	Train newly registered OOPPs to submit individual-level dispensing data through the Naloxone Dispensing Form (NDF); support OOPPs as they integrate form submission into their workflows; monitor form submission and provide support to OOPPs to increase their response rate.   •	Manage timely entry of monthly distribution reports into database; reconcile naloxone fulfillment with monthly data; manage timely preparation of report materials for data processing  •	Develop and refine surveys, RedCap forms, and other dispensing data collection forms as needed.  •	Collaborate with NYS Department of Health AIDS Institute, the Overdose Prevention Coordinator, the Naloxone Inventory Coordinator, and other BADUPCT staff to maintain registration and contact information for all OOPPs  •	Provide timely response to requests for naloxone fulfillment and dispensing data, naloxone reversals and other relevant information  •	Refine systems, as needed, for tracking naloxone dispensing data   •	Support Naloxone Inventory Coordinator in the packaging of naloxone kits  •	Participate in Overdose Prevention Unit meetings, including facilitation on a rotating basis; provide administrative support to the Overdose Prevention Unit including scheduling meetings, developing agendas, and other tasks as needed.  •	Participate in agency-wide activities for advancing racial, gender, and social equity.  •	Other duties or tasks may be assigned on an as-needed basis  Preferred Skills:   •	Knowledge of substance use issues and harm reduction practice and theory, including syringe exchange, overdose prevention and education for HIV and Hepatitis C prevention. •	Experience with quantitative data, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize epidemiologic and other scientific literature. •	Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Possess exceptional interpersonal, research, written and verbal communication skills.  •	The candidate will also be detail-oriented with outstanding organizational skills.  •	Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced, high volume environment.  •	Proficiency in Excel, Access, Word, and PowerPoint. •	Experience querying or managing data using code, such as SQL, SAS, or R. jobs.title: One Health Analyst, Bureau of Communicable Diseases
jobs.description: The Bureau of Communicable Diseases (BCD), part of the Division of Disease Control, is responsible for the surveillance, prevention, and control of over 70 infectious diseases including foodborne, enteric, waterborne, respiratory, zoonotic and vector-borne diseases. You will assist the Antimicrobial Resistance Unit and the One Health team by providing dedicated analytical support to monitor and control multi drug resistant organisms in humans and animals in New York City. Within BCD, the Antimicrobial Resistance Unit (ARU) aims to 1) conduct surveillance for and facilitate rapid response to high-priority multidrug-resistant organisms, 2) undertake epidemiologic research on the transmission of these organisms in the community, and 3) promote judicious antibiotic prescribing practices and infection prevention efforts by disseminating resources to NYC stakeholders, including data on local antibiotic use and resistance trends. The ARU is comprised of three teams: the Surveillance and Data team, the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) and Antimicrobial Stewardship (AS) team, and the One Health team. The goals of the One Health team are to understand and control the spread of multidrug-resistant organisms in humans, animals, and our shared environment.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Under the supervision of the One Health team lead, this analyst will provide data support for both the One Health team specifically as well as the ARU more broadly. Their duties will include, but are not limited to:  • Building, maintaining, and strengthening surveillance of antimicrobial resistance and antimicrobial use data from humans and animals.  • Supporting IPC and AS for veterinary professionals including creating new and innovative resources. • Providing analytical support for whole genome sequencing (WGS) initiatives, including: o Coordinating with epidemiology, laboratory, informatics, and information technology teams to ensure proper transmission of WGS data.  o Developing and maintaining routine reports to analyze and share WGS data. • Providing analytical support for ARU projects including:  o Surveillance of carbapenem-resistant organisms (CRO) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in New York City and detection of community-associated transmission  o Core ARU duties and data needs such as CRO case investigations, routine data cleaning, quality assurance activities, etc. • Supporting project management needs based on data analytics.  • Presenting results of data analyses to internal and external stakeholders. Grounded in a commitment to equity, the CYF-DD's mission is to promote the mental health of all children, youth and families and to empower individuals with developmental disabilities to lead integrated and fulfilling lives. To achieve this, we work to improve policies, plan and fund services, conduct research and evaluation, support community based partners and connect children and youth to needed services. jobs.title: Program & Data Manager, CHSC, Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorkers. The Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health (Harlem BNH) supports the agency's mission to protect and promote the health of all New Yorkers. Harlem BNH catchment area includes the entire community of Harlem, including East, Central and West Harlem as well as Washington Heights and Inwood. Harlem BNH focuses on the structural and root causes of health disparity outcomes and develop programs to address these outcomes with input from partners and residents. Addressing the social determinants of health (SDOH), is a key focus point and is enshrined in programs such as the Harlem Health Advocacy Partnership and the Asthma Counselor Program. Other Bureau offerings include a variety of programs and activities focused on the health and wellness of Harlem residents. The Harlem Bureau also houses the East and Central Harlem Neighborhood Health Action Center, which is a key part of the NYC's effort to promote health equity and reduce health disparities in the neighborhood. The Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health seeks to hire a Program & Data Manager, Creating Healthy Schools & Communities (CHSC) to be the senior programmatic and operational lead for the Harlem Bureau of Neighborhood Health's CHSC programs, a NYS Department of Health funded initiative. The program focuses on integrated school- and community-based strategies that advance chronic disease prevention, physical activity, nutrition access, and health equity.   DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO:  Systems Building & Data Management:  - Oversee data collection, monitoring, and reporting for programmatic, community engagement, and evaluation activities.  - Identify and disseminate best practices.  - Utilize Public Health Partners Connect and other Harlem Bureau data systems to track participation, partnerships, and outcomes.  - Integrate CHSC data with broader Harlem Bureau reporting systems.  - Prepare reports, dashboards and presentations for internal teams, funders and external partners.  - Present neighborhood health data to partners to inform shared strategies and collective action.   Community & School Partnership Development:  - Develop and maintain strong relationships with schools, community-based organizations, city and state agencies, and local community leaders.  - Build and support coalitions to leverage resources, strengthen coordination, and increase program sustainability.  - Provide training and technical assistance to partners implementing CHSC-aligned activities.   Program Implementation & Grant Management:  - Serve as programmatic and operational lead for day-to-day planning, implementation and monitoring of CHSC within Harlem Bureau.  - Manage all grant-related activities including budgeting, reporting, contracting, staffing and compliance.  - Translate grant deliverables into actionable workplans aligned with Bureau and community-wide priorities.  - Support program sustainability and continuous improvement efforts.  - Coordinate vendors, facilitators and partners supporting physical activity, nutrition and wellness initiatives.  - Support integrated school-community programming that reflects neighborhood needs and lived experience.  - Manage staff. - Complete special projects and initiatives.  - Represent Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health at meetings as needed. It is expected that the position will work 35 hours per week to help coordinate grant related activities, track progress on grant milestones, support cross-bureau programmatic coordination, and assist with sustainability initiatives and other projects. jobs.title: Program Manager, Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorker. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems and the Bureau of Finance, Administration and Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race To Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The NYC Health Department's Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention (BDCP) strives to reduce the burden of chronic disease, including heart disease, diabetes, and cancer, among New Yorkers. BCDP focuses on nutrition, tobacco use, the built environment, and reducing the impact of cancer. BCDP aims to advance evidence-based policies, programs, community engagement, and research aimed at shifting environments, changing systems and promoting health equity. As a bureau within the NYC Health Department's Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW), BCDP contributes to CHECW's goal of eliminating racial inequities and reducing overall premature mortality among New Yorkers. BCDP puts a focus on reducing exposure to and consumption of unhealthy foods and tobacco industry products and countering industry practices that negatively impact health. In addition to pursuing population-level approaches, BCDP prioritizes communities that bear a disproportionate burden of chronic disease.   The Active Design Unit within BCDP seeks to hire a Program Manager, the Program Manager will oversee the implementation and day to day management of the unit's place-based programs in schools and neighborhood settings, including program planning, partnership coordination, research, and evaluation activities.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Oversee and implement place-based program projects that advance the goals of the Active Design Unit and BCDP, in close collaboration with community-based organizations, government agencies, consultants, and other external partners.  • In collaboration with unit Director, manage and oversee programmatic budgets, contracts, and procurement.  • Manage strategic relationships with peer city agencies, community organizations, academic institutions, and other external partners to share information, coordinate activities, and collaborate on projects that support and inform the work of the Active Design Unit.  • Support community engagement and partner coordination throughout program planning and implementation, including activities that incorporate community perspectives and lived experience into Active Design projects.  • Prepare program updates, grant proposals, funder progress reports, and other written materials to communicate program activities, accomplishments, and outcomes.  • Supervise and manage staff and other team members as assigned, providing guidance, setting priorities, and overseeing work assignments.  • Conduct research and review public health and built environment literature to inform the design and implementation of evidence-informed initiatives that leverage urban planning, architecture, and design strategies to promote healthy behaviors and improve health outcomes.  • Coordinate with Bureau and agency colleagues and external city agency and private partners to plan and implement research and evaluation activities in support of Active Design programs and strategic initiatives.  • Support the development and implementation of data collection and evaluation protocols to document program implementation, participation, utilization, and outcomes, and contribute to analyses, reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. • Monitor and synthesize emerging research, best practices, and public policy developments related to the built environment, physical activity, mental health, social connection, and other health outcomes, particularly in school and neighborhood se tings.  • Plan and coordinate meetings and events, including developing event logistics, preparing presentations and other materials, and communicating program information to key audiences.  • Contribute to the development of reports, publications, presentations, and other knowledge-sharing materials that communicate best practices and practical strategies for integrating Active Design into school and neighborhood settings.  • Perform additional duties as needed. jobs.title: Program Quality Manager, Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and STI
jobs.description: The NYC Health Department’s Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (BHHS) falls within the Division of Disease Control, oversees the City's response to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Its mission is to improve the lives of New Yorkers by ending transmission, illness, stigma, and inequities related to viral hepatitis, HIV, and STIs. BHHS does this through testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming; epidemiology and surveillance; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiatives. BHHS’s over 500 staff members work across eight programs: Administration, HIV Care and Treatment, HIV Epidemiology, HIV Prevention, Policy and External Affairs, Racial Equity and Social Justice Initiatives, STI, and Viral Hepatitis. The Viral Hepatitis Program conducts surveillance, and develops and implements programs and projects to prevent, manage and treat hepatitis B and C in New York City.   Reporting to the Project Director and working with the Capacity Building unit, you will be assigned specific viral hepatitis linkage to care initiatives and strategies addressing the Plan to Eliminate Viral Hepatitis in New York City by 2030. Under direction of the Project Director and Director of Capacity Building, you will develop, implement, and evaluate program activities; meeting with external organization staff (such as program managers, clinicians, and service providers) to understand their program implementation and service delivery needs; and provide tailored technical assistance to support effective program outcomes.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Monitor contracts and budgets ensuring timely and accurate invoicing in compliance with agency policies and procedures. • Plan and coordinate with contractors the implementation of linkage to care initiatives program model and evidence-based practices (using Salesforce, MS Teams and Planner. • Analyze program data and conduct quality assurance (using REDCap, SAS, Tableau, MS Forms). • Engage collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to address service delivery needs and improve program outcomes. • Develop, implement and evaluate quality improvement projects to increase viral hepatitis screening, linkage to care, and treatment rates. • Conduct comprehensive literature reviews and critically evaluate health research studies to support implementation of evidence-based strategies and interventions. • Stay up to date on the latest trends, developments and innovations related to viral hepatitis screening, linkage to care, treatment and relevant topics such as immigration and substance use to enhance overall effectiveness of the program. • Contribute to the development and dissemination of program protocols, resources and tools to support program outcomes. • Maintain accurate records and prepare reports. • Support the dissemination of program findings, including for presentations and manuscripts. • Supervise one or two staff. • Contribute to Capacity Building and Viral Hepatitis Program activities. • Contribute to the Bureau’s racial justice and health equity activities. • Complete other tasks as assigned. jobs.description: The Bureau of Equitable Health System is the healthcare systems bureau of Department of Health & Mental Hygiene.  Our mission is to apply policy, evidence, and practical expertise to improve equity in health care delivery at the individual, organizational, and systems levels.  We do this by engaging primary care providers and other healthcare organizations to implement evidence-based strategies; leveraging information to support planning and technical assistance for providers and payers; advancing policy to close the racial equity gap for priority health outcomes; and surfacing opportunities where health care can influence and connect consumers to social support and addressing the whole person, beyond physical ailments. Practice Transformation and Technical Assistance: •	Manage a small portfolio of Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) and related practice transformation initiatives. •	Provide consultative and technical assistance support to participating practices related to care delivery redesign, care coordination workflows, and population health interventions. •	Contribute to the development and refinement of practice transformation curricula, tools, and guidance materials. Supervision, Training, and Knowledge Sharing: •	Provide technical guidance and mentoring to facilitators and project staff engaged in research, evaluation, and practice transformation activities. •	Supervise staff in matrixed project assignments, as directed. •	Develop and deliver trainings, presentations, and infor •	Develop and deliver trainings, presentations, and informational sessions for internal and external audiences. •	Communicate technical information clearly and effectively in both written and verbal formats. Vendor and Stakeholder Coordination: •	Assist in the coordination of contracts and deliverables with external vendors supporting research, evaluation, or implementation activities. •	Monitor vendor deliverables and support review of invoices and documentation. •	Liaise with internal and external stakeholders to support coordinated implementation efforts. Additional Duties: •	Assist with the preparation of grant and funding application materials, including project descriptions and evaluation components. •	Perform related duties as assigned. jobs.title: Public Health Assistant, Data Entry
jobs.description: ONLY PERMANENT EMPLOYEES IN THE TITLE AND THOSE THAT ARE REACHABLE ON THE PUBLIC HEALTH ASSISTANT (SH) CIVIL SERVICE LIST ARE ELIGIBLE TO APPLY.  Division/Program Summary:  The Division of Family and Child Health, Office of School Health (OSH) Vision Program provides mandated vision screening services to Pre-K, kindergarten and first grade students throughout the five boroughs of New York City. The Vision Program is partnered with Warby Parker, a manufacturer and retailer of prescription eyeglasses. jobs.title: Senior Drug Checking Epidemiologist, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADU develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities. The Office of Research, Surveillance, Policy and Communications within the Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use is responsible for conducting timely surveillance of alcohol and drug-related morbidity and mortality in NYC, reporting on key trends and disparate impacts by demographic group and neighborhood, conducting drug-checking services and surveillance of the unregulated drug supply in NYC, performing program evaluation and monitoring, and leading community engagement and communications campaigns to educate New Yorkers about alcohol and drug-related health risks.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: 1. Serve as data steward for all drug checking data. 2. Extract, clean, manipulate, organize, and analyze data for the bureau’s Drug Checking Program using primarily R, REDCap, Excel and other platforms as needed. 3. Design, conduct, and develop new methods of analyses that will inform future directions of the Drug Checking Program. 4. Create and update data management documentation relating to the Drug Checking Program, including data dictionaries and codebooks, protocols, and methods. 5. Lead preparation and dissemination of data tables, reports, briefs, presentations, and scientific manuscripts to clearly communicate findings and recommendations to a variety of audiences including the public, agency and bureau leadership, other government agencies, and healthcare providers. 6. Lead the development of data visualization and public dissemination of drug checking results collected across New York City sites. 7. Prepare and manage IRB applications for the Drug Checking Program. 8. Represent bureau in collaborations with internal and external partners, and collaborate to align data collection and reporting with bureau monitoring and policy needs. 9. Supervise and mentor the work of a Drug Checking Data Analyst. 10. Perform all other responsibilities and projects as assigned by supervisors. jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality. With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorkers. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems, the Bureau of Finance and Administrative Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race to Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The Health Department launched Race to Justice (RTJ) in 2016 as its agency-wide internal transformation initiative. The primary purpose of the initiative is to build the Health Department's capacity to address structural racism and health inequities by promoting anti racism and embedding racial equity and social justice in our policies, processes, and programs, ensuring that our internal and external practices reflect our values without perpetuating injustices. Spearheaded by the RTJMT, the initiative aims to transform the Health Department by building capacity and embedding racial equity and social justice within every aspect of DOHMH to ultimately improve equitable health outcomes for all New Yorkers by: 1) Increasing staff's awareness of how racism and other intersecting systems of oppression operate within institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, including the Health Department, are not separate and immune from these systemic injustices. 2) Developing staff's skills to address how internal systems of oppression create health equities. 3) Examining how structural racism and other intersecting systems of oppression impact the Health Department's work, decisions, interactions, and priorities. 4) Implementing policies and practices to mitigate the impacts of systems of oppression.   The Office of the Chief Equity Officer seeks to hire a Senior Manager of Capacity Building to join the management team to build internal capacity among staff to advance racial and social justice and the Health Department's equity goals. jobs.description: The New York City (NYC) Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) is a public health leader serving over 8.4 million New York City residents from diverse ethnic, cultural, and economic backgrounds. The NYC Public Health Laboratory (PHL) is one of the largest local public health laboratories in the United States offering a dynamic and innovative work environment where employees contribute to the health and safety of NYC residents by providing clinical and environmental laboratory testing services. With more than 100 years of leadership in public health, a team of over 200 scientific and support staff are committed to its mission to safeguard the health of all NYC residents by providing quality laboratory testing services that support the priorities of the NYC DOHMH and its community partners to prevent and respond to clinical and environmental public health concerns.   The DOHMH PHL seeks a qualified candidate to serve as a supervisor in the Environmental Sciences Section. This position will play an integral role in laboratory testing and responding to public health threats, including but not limited to COVID-19, vaccine preventable diseases, HIV, Legionella as well as respiratory, foodborne, and waterborne disease outbreaks. This is an excellent opportunity to join our multidisciplinary team, and collaborate with local, state, federal, and academic partners. The supervisor will primarily work within the Water Microbiology Unit at PHL. The units utilize microbiological and molecular microbiological tools to detect and monitor pathogens in drinking and recreational water, and non-potable water systems such as cooling towers. This includes NYC’s beach monitoring and Legionella response programs. ·   DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Supervising, training, assigning work, and evaluating the performance of staff. Able to shift priorities in response to rapidly evolving work environment. • Conducting investigations regarding agents related to public health outbreaks using independent judgement and initiative, and performing data analysis on test results. Assisting in the coordination of agency, local and federal partners in investigations. • Performing research to identify and implement new technologies. • Communicating effectively with lab technologists and internal and external partners. • Evaluating data, preparing reports, maintaining records, and assisting in the coordination of research efforts of the Agency. • Maintaining and participating in a program of quality control and assurance; and advising staff on appropriate methods and techniques. • Implementing and monitoring laboratory quality, and health and safety policies and procedures. • Performing or overseeing the design and maintenance of charts, logs, and other records. • Assist with inventory, budgeting, and procurement to ensure that laboratory is properly stocked with reagents and supplies necessary for testing; and ensure that items are properly tracked using inventory management system. • Writes original manuscripts for publication based on data analyses. jobs.title: Team Lead: TST for SU & EAU, Bureau of Tuberculosis Control
jobs.description: The Team Lead for TST (SU & EAU) directs tuberculosis surveillance, environmental infection control, and outbreak prevention strategies across DOH chest centers, shelters, and high-risk facilities. In this role, you will manage a multidisciplinary team of research scientists, epidemiologists, and public health advisors conducting quantitative research on airborne tuberculosis detection, managing employee tuberculin skin testing (TST) programs, and overseeing patient isolation protocols. You will evaluate airborne mitigation technologies—such as UVGI, negative pressure, and ACH air-flow systems—to recommend compliant products and establish evidence-based safety guidelines. Additionally, you will oversee outbreak investigations, represent the TB Control Program across internal and external committees, and author scientific papers to publish findings and advance environmental infection control practices statewide.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Direct activities and staff of the Tuberculin Skin Testing (TST) Surveillance Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. Ensures that staff in the TST Unit conduct periodic and serial testing of targeted high-risk DOH employees. - Direct activities and staff of the Environmental Affairs Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. - Directs respiratory protection fit testing by the TST Unit and the Environmental Affairs Unit for designated staff in BTBC. - Performs employee evaluations - Serve as a resource to the BTBC for environmental issues pertaining to TB infection control devices and measures including UVG lamps, negatives air pressure, ventilation, and respiratory prevention. - Consults on referrals for patients on home isolation - Provides specialty guidance to Bureau and DOH staff associated with TB outbreaks. - Directs TB related infection control surveys, evaluation, and assessments. - The Senior Investigative Analyst will work closely with the Director of IMPACT to identify appropriate cases for pre-arrest investigation, support the development of those investigations, coordinate with internal and external partners, assist in creating and implementing protocols for this new initiative, and maintain and analyze program data. The Analyst will also regularly represent IMPACT and the Office in meetings with the New York City Police Department (NYPD), community-based organizations, and other bureaus and units within the District Attorney’s Office. The position also includes assisting with U visa law enforcement certifications, providing exposure to the intersection of criminal, civil, and immigration law. This position offers a unique opportunity to help shape and implement a new initiative, gain experience with both criminal and civil matters, develop an understanding of immigration law through U visa certification work, and collaborate closely with prosecutors, law enforcement, survivor advocates, community organizations, and other partners.   Responsibilities include but are not limited to:  •	Collaborating closely with the Director of IMPACT to review criminal complaints, domestic incident reports, police reports, and other materials submitted by the New York City Police Department and identify cases appropriate for IMPACT intervention and pre-arrest investigation. •	Assisting with pre-arrest investigations by obtaining and reviewing evidence, generating subpoenas and other records requests, analyzing documents and digital materials, and conducting searches of relevant databases. •	Coordinating with the Survivor Services Bureau by providing advocates with relevant survivors and case information to facilitate survivor outreach and the scheduling of interviews. •	Attending survivor and witness interviews to take detailed notes, assist with case documentation, identify necessary investigative follow-up, and support the development of the investigation. •	Serving as a regular liaison with NYPD personnel, documenting, implementing, and refining policies, protocols, workflows, and best practices for IMPACT as the initiative develops and expands. •	Partnering with advocates from the Survivor Services reviewing case records and related materials to determine whether a matter involves qualifying criminal activity, preparing certification forms and supporting documentation, communicating with immigration attorneys and other relevant parties, and tracking requests through completion. •	Tracking, organizing, and maintaining comprehensive data regarding referrals, investigations, case outcomes, survivor engagement, services, and other IMPACT activities. •	Conducting data collection and analysis to identify trends, measure program activity and outcomes, and support evaluation and continued development of IMPACT. •	Preparing statistical reports, summaries, charts, Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, and other materials for internal and external reporting, presentations, program evaluation, and strategic planning. •	Compiling and organizing discovery and other case materials to ensure accurate and timely preparation for legal proceedings. •	Drafting correspondence, memoranda, legal documents, protocols, reports, and other written materials with accuracy and attention to detail. •	Assisting with the development and delivery of training, presentations, and informational materials for NYPD, community partners, and Office personnel regarding IMPACT. •	Supporting special projects and other operational needs of IMPACT as the initiative continues to develop and expand. jobs.description: The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) is the largest Fire Department in the United States and universally is recognized as the world's busiest and most highly skilled emergency response agency. The Department's main goal is to provide fire protection, emergency medical care, and other critical public safety services to residents and visitors in the five boroughs. FDNY members are sworn to serve and protect life and property and the Department works to continually educate the public in fire, life safety and disaster preparedness, along with enforcing public safety codes. Since its inception in 1865, FDNY has helped lead efforts to make New York the safest big city in the nation. This accomplishment requires a steadfast and daily commitment to maintaining the Department's core values.  The FDNY Bureau of Enterprise Technology manages key departmental initiatives and drives data-driven decision-making. Its Data Quality unit is responsible for generating actionable insights through analysis, reporting, and visualizations. This unit also ensures accountability and transparency by compiling metrics for the Mayor's Management Report (MMR) and producing datasets for NYC Open Data.  The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) seeks a full-time City Research Scientist, L2 in the Data Quality Unit. With latitude for independent initiative and judgement, the Data Quality Analyst will assist the Department’s in the making evidence-based decisions. Day-to-day responsibilities focus on data quality and insight delivery. This includes rigorously performing data quality checks and anomaly detection. The Data Quality Analyst will also support the building of interactive dashboards, primarily using Tableau and modern Python frameworks (Dash/Streamlit). Other core duties include swift fulfilling of ad-hoc data requests and designing appropriate metrics to track and report on departmental performance. This position will also participate in community outreach, especially in the context of Open Data which could include responding to public inquiries, representing the Department at Open Data Events and gathering feedback from the community. This is a crucial function that connects the FDNY's internal data efforts with the public, leveraging data transparency to enhance safety and build trust. Minimum qualifications: 1. A doctorate degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and one year of full-time experience in a responsible supervisory, administrative or research capacity in the appropriate field of specialization; or  2. A master's degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and three years of responsible full-time research experience in the appropriate field of specialization; or  3. jobs.description: Who We Are Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms. We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes. We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact. What We Build Our products— Eureka Math and Eureka Math², Wit & Wisdom , Geodes , and the newly launched Arts & Letters ELA —are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide. Eureka Math is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application. Wit & Wisdom® and Arts & Letters ELA™ anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. Geodes® complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy. These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students. Where We’re Headed Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support. Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale. Job Purpose Reporting to the Director of Policy, the Lead Policy Analyst will act as a senior-level individual contributor, operating as the team’s primary subject matter expert and analytical engine. This role will take ownership of Great Minds’ policy intelligence work by tracking and interpreting the federal, state, and local landscape to ensure the organization is well-positioned to engage and influence. The position will bring depth, initiative, and independent judgment to complex policy questions and will translate findings into strategies that meaningfully shape how Great Minds engages with policymakers, state agencies, and K–12 stakeholders. Responsibilities Serve as the team’s primary analytical resource for K–12 policy trends—independently framing issues, synthesizing intelligence across federal, state, and local levels, and contributing substantively to Great Minds’ company-wide point of view on factors shaping the adoption and implementation of high-quality instructional materials. Own the tracking and monitoring of state and local legislation and policy; identify and escalate emerging policy trends with clear analytical context and recommended implications for the organization. Lead projects that examine how legislative mandates shape policy action at the local, regional, and state levels; develop findings that are rigorous, accessible, and directly connected to Great Minds’ strategic priorities. Translate regional trend analysis into concrete recommendations that help shape the organization’s policy engagement strategy; identifying where and how Great Minds should invest, focus and build relationships. Ensure internal stakeholders are equipped to understand and act on the policy environment by producing clear briefings, frameworks, and recommendations tailored to diverse audiences across the organization. Represent Great Minds externally at policy conferences and sector events, strengthening the organization’s credibility and visibility among policymakers and K–12 influencers. Requirements 7+ years of experience in K–12 policy, applied research, or a closely related discipline, with a track record of owning and advancing substantive policy work Proven ability to independently drive research projects from problem framing through strategic recommendation, with strong judgment about when to escalate and how to prioritize Sophisticated command of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies, with the ability to synthesize complex findings into accessible, compelling narratives for varied audiences Proven ability to manage competing priorities and stakeholder demands, balancing ongoing policy monitoring with discrete research projects and time-sensitive requests from across the organization Deep familiarity with state and local policy development processes, including legislative tracking and stakeholder engagement Demonstrated experience converting a complex policy landscape into clear strategic priorities and actionable plans Required Education Bachelor’s degree Preferred Advanced degree in public policy, education policy, or a related field Status Full-time Location Remote The expected base salary range for this position is $107,000-$120,000, however the offered salary may be higher or lower than the above range dependent on numerous factors including, but not limited to location, work experience, skills and internal equity considerations. The base salary is not inclusive of benefits or other incentives. A cover letter and resume are required to be considered for this position. New employees will be required to successfully complete a background check. Any communication to applicants relating to the Great Minds hiring process will only come from email addresses with the domains greatminds.org or greatminds.recruitee.com . If in the course of the application or hiring process with Great Minds you are contacted through another domain, are requested to provide banking or other sensitive information, or you note any other suspicious activity, please contact security@greatminds.org Great Minds is an equal opportunity employer. We will extend equal opportunity to all individuals without regard to race, religion, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, disability, age, genetic information, or any other status protected under applicable federal, state, or local laws. Our policy reflects and affirms the organization’s commitment to the principles of fair employment and the elimination of all discriminatory practices. #LI-Remote

jobs.description: About the Agency:  The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.  Your Team:  The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. As part of OPS, the Division of Strategic Operations and Analytics (SOA) works to increase HPD's impact by analyzing and improving operations agency-wide. SOA does this by clarifying HPD program missions, objectives, and stakeholders; implementing initiatives that advance HPD's goals; analyzing data to deliver actionable insights to HPD programs; and increasing the agency's overall ability to leverage data.  Your Impact:  As the Analytics & Reporting Engineer within SOA, you will play a key role in making HPD’s data more accessible, reliable, and reusable to support reporting and analytics. By building well-structured datasets, automations and data flows, you will help SOA and other HPD offices turn data into key reporting and metrics that support key agency programs for New Yorkers.   Your Role:  Your role will focus on hands-on development of data pipelines, curating datasets and data flows in SQL Server and building reusable scripts and code to support reporting and analytics work for agency programs such as homeless placement services, homebuyer assistance, housing distress & compliance, and fair housing work. You will also create and maintain reports and dashboards, or related dataflows/models. Exercising independent judgement and initiative, you will implement solutions through scalable data models, automated workflows, and well-structured datasets and BI data flows - to enable more efficient reporting, research, and analytics for key agency programs.   Your Responsibilities:  •	Build and maintain core datasets, data models, and dashboards to support key program reporting and analytics •	Build and automate Python-based data cleaning and integration pipelines — merging data across siloed source systems and using automation tools — to support reporting needs for housing placements, fair housing and more. •	Load cleaned datasets into SQL Server and connect to BI tools (e.g. Power BI) to support reporting/dashboarding. •	Implement basic code validation, testing, and documentation practices to keep analytics scripts and datasets reliable and maintainable. •	Document code standards and workflows so datasets and scripts remain usable/maintainable by the team over time. •	Apply data engineering skills and creative collaboration techniques to address technical issues and drive the approach for the team   Preferred skills   •	Inquisitive, self-motivated problem-solver who is passionate about making organizations more data-driven •	Comfortable working in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment with messy data and legacy systems; motivated by rolling up your sleeves and building practical tools that make a real impact on people's lives. •	Experience building or supporting data pipelines (ETL/ELT) — extracting, cleaning, and transforming data from multiple sources. •	Experience working with relational databases (e.g., SQL Server or similar) •	Some experience with BI data modeling (preferably Power BI or similar) is a plus •	Familiarity with source control and version control workflows (e.g., Azure DevOps Repos) •	Strong interpersonal and organizational skills; able to ask thoughtful questions and collaborate across teams •	Strong aptitude for learning new tools and technologies independently using online resources •	Technical skills: SQL, Python, Power BI data modeling (DAX, Power Query M), and data modeling fundamentals Minimum qualifications: 1. jobs.title: Compliance Specialist, Lead Hazard Control & Healthy Homes
jobs.description: About the Agency:  The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.   As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike. [GS1.1]    Your Team The Compliance Specialist for Lead Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will be a key member of the Compliance & Strategy team within the agency’s Office of Compliance & Risk Management (CRM). This Office includes various compliance, oversight, and hearing functions to ensure fairness, consistency, and equity in both our external and internal engagement. CRM collaborates with programs across HPD to ensure the agency and its partners comply with laws (federal, state, and city), regulatory requirements, policies, and procedures. CRM includes the following Divisions and units: •	Compliance & Strategy •	Economic Opportunity & Regulatory Compliance •	Audit Support   •	Adjudications •	Public Information  Your Impact CRM is responsible for overseeing the agency’s compliance and risk management functions, liaising with the units and staff responsible for relevant compliance responsibilities, audit responses, site standard adherence for financed construction work, public-facing appeals and hearings, and managing risk for the agency. The Compliance Specialist for Lead Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will have the opportunity to use their expertise to provide leadership and technical assistance in support of health and safety requirements and compliance best practices throughout the agency, with a focus on environmental hazards. This role will also provide a unique opportunity to help strengthen agency compliance culture and ensure compliance is seamlessly incorporated into HPD program administration and operations.  Your Role Reporting to the Executive Director of Compliance & Strategy, the Compliance Specialist for Lead-Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will manage cross-agency compliance of regulatory requirements and strengthen agency compliance by assessing risks and providing technical assistance and guidance to staff throughout the agency. The person in this role will focus on agency program compliance with existing, new, and revised laws and regulations related to lead-based paint, radon, mold, asthma triggers, carbon monoxide, and other health and safety hazards. The person in this role will work closely and liaise with Offices throughout HPD, including Enforcement & Neighborhood Services (ENS), Housing Access & Stability (HAS), Asset & Property Management (APM), Development (OOD), Policy & Strategy (OPS), Finance & Administration (OFA), and Legal Affairs (OLA) for effective monitoring, tracking, and strengthening of relevant agency compliance functions.   Your Responsibilities The Compliance Specialist for Lead Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will provide agency-wide programmatic support to strengthen compliance with federal, state, and local health and safety hazard requirements. This includes, but is not limited to: •	Evaluate the implementation of lead- and healthy homes-related procedures across all areas of the agency including: o	Coordinate compliance monitoring related to requirements under federal, state, and local laws, including 24 CFR Part 35, Title X of the Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act; Local Law 1 (2004), 66 (2019), Local Law 31 (2020), Local Law 111 (2023), Local Law 122 (2023), and Local Law 123 (2023), as well as Local Law 55 (2018) and other regulations related to indoor allergens such as mold and pests. o	Participate in monitoring's and/or audits Work with staff in the Offices of Enforcement & Neighborhood Services (ENS), Development, Asset & Property Management (APM), Housing Access & Stability (HAS), Neighborhood Strategies (ONS), and others to coordinate, document, and strengthen, as needed, lead and Healthy Homes hazard compliance. •	Perform assessments and evaluations to proactively identify risk areas and program noncompliance. Provide corrective action plans, recommendations, and a set of best practices, as necessary to mitigate risks. •	Participate in the development of agency-wide trainings related to lead-based paint, Healthy Homes, and other relevant healthy and safety topics. •	Support the development of internal reporting mechanisms for specialized initiatives for public reporting. •	Monitor regulatory changes and keep stakeholders abreast of operational or other implications. •	Assist with other Compliance & Strategy special projects and compliance priorities as needed.  A cover letter is required. [NJ2.1]Please submit a cover letter as part of your application.   Required Skills and Qualifications •	Demonstrated ability to interpret complex legislation, regulations, and policy requirements, and translate them into clear operational guidance and practical implementation approaches •	Strong attention to detail and excellent organizational and problem-solving abilities •	Strong collaborator across all levels of management and experience, and with a wide array of internal and external stakeholders •	Ability to balance a variety of projects and priorities for a fast-paced, high-volume workload •	Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal and communication skills (verbal and written)  Preferred Skills and Qualifications •	Knowledge of New York City’s Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention Act of 2003, also known as Local Law 1 of 2004 (LL1), Local Law 55 of 2018, Title X and 24 CFR Part 35 (Lead-Based Paint Poisoning Prevention in Certain Residential Structures), and other related legal and regulatory requirements.   •	Experience in the lead-based paint or mold fields, particularly related to project, staff, and vendor management •	Work in housing, environmental health and regulatory compliance frequently incorporates applied social science research skills, including data analysis, program evaluation and evidence-based policy implementation. jobs.title: Data Analyst for the Division of Housing Opportunity
jobs.description: About the Agency:  The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.    As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.   Your Team:   The Office of Housing Access and Stability (HAS) consists of the divisions of Housing Opportunities & Program Services, Tenant and Owner Resources, Housing Stability, Budget and Program Operations, and Program Policy and Innovation. Our mission of the office is to ensure fair, efficient, and transparent access to affordable housing. HAS provides subsidies, placement services, and tools that connect New Yorkers to affordable housing and ensures vulnerable households in subsidized housing have the support they need to be safely housed. Housing Access is committed to expanding housing choices, affirmatively furthering fair housing, and stabilizing the financial health of buildings.  The Division of Housing Opportunity & Program Services ensures that HPD’s affordable housing is made available through fair, transparent, and accessible programming. Developers creating affordable housing are required to offer many types of units through an open lottery process on NYC Housing Connect and fill other units through a placement process for households in the City’s shelter system. Housing Opportunity & Program Services administers the housing lottery and homeless placements programs and crafts policy and procedures to ensure that these programs offer equal opportunity to all applicants and affirmatively further fair housing.  Your Impact:  As the Data Analyst for the Homeless Placement Services (HPS) Unit within the Division of Housing Opportunity (DHO), you will support data management, reporting, performance metrics, and project intake activities for the unit, while also providing data and analytical support to the broader Division. The position will play a key role in ensuring the accuracy, timeliness, and integrity of data used to monitor HPS operations and inform program and agency decision-making. The position will also serve as a cross-functional resource for project intake and onboarding, working with managing agents and internal staff to ensure that new projects and units are properly entered, inspected, and ready for lease-up and assignment.  Your Role:  The Data Analyst will support the development, maintenance, analysis, and reporting of data related to HPS operations and DHO priorities. The position will produce and maintain reports and performance metrics used by unit and division leadership to monitor workload, production, outcomes, and operational performance. In addition, the position will support the project intake process, including entering new projects into the appropriate systems, serving as a liaison with managing agents, monitoring project readiness, and coordinating to ensure that required inspections and other prerequisites are completed before units are made available for lease-up and assignment to the HPS team. The position will also provide data and analytical support to other teams within DHO, including assisting with divisional reporting, data requests, special projects, data quality initiatives, and other analytical needs as assigned.  Your Responsibilities:  •	Maintain tracking systems and databases used to monitor HPS projects, units, assignments, referrals, placements, and other program activities. •	Generate, analyze, and distribute internal and external reports regarding unit targets, workload, production, placements, and other key performance metrics. •	Develop and maintain performance metrics and reporting tools used by HPS and DHO leadership to monitor program and operational performance. •	Analyze data to identify trends, patterns, discrepancies, and opportunities for process improvement. •	Respond to data and reporting requests from HPS and DHO leadership and staff. •	Provide data, reporting, and analytical support to other teams within DHO as needed. •	Assist with divisional data projects, reporting initiatives, special analyses, and other data-related assignments. •	Ensure data integrity and accuracy across Access, Excel, SharePoint, and other reporting and tracking systems. •	Perform routine database and reporting system maintenance to ensure alignment with changes in business processes and program requirements. •	Work with staff to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve data quality and reporting issues. •	Collaborate with staff to identify and correct data entry errors and discrepancies. •	Support the project intake process by entering new projects and related information into HPS systems and tracking platforms. •	Serve as a liaison with managing agents during the project intake and onboarding process. •	Coordinate with managing agents and internal staff to monitor project readiness and ensure required inspections and other prerequisites are completed before units are made available for lease-up and assignment to the HPS team. •	Monitor project and unit information to ensure that data is complete, accurate, and current throughout the intake and placement process. •	Coordinate and share information with the Department of Social Services (DSS) and HPD program areas to support accurate and timely referrals and placements. •	Assist with the management of a portfolio of homeless set-aside and/or 421-a homeless units, including providing referrals and tracking placements, as necessary. •	Develop and maintain documentation, procedures, and other resources supporting consistent data management, reporting, and program operations. •	Complete special projects, analyses, and reports requested by the Assistant Commissioner, Director, Deputy Director, Team Leaders, and other DHO leadership. •	Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to resolve data, reporting, project intake, and operational issues. •	Provide cross-functional support to the HPS Unit and DHO as needed. •	Perform other related duties as assigned to support the goals and priorities of HPS and DHO.  Preferred skills:  ¿	Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. ¿	Demonstrated experience developing, maintaining, and analyzing reports and performance metrics. ¿	Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint. ¿	Experience maintaining databases, tracking systems, and reporting tools. ¿	Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and integrity. ¿	Ability to identify trends, patterns, discrepancies, and opportunities to improve business processes. ¿	Strong written and verbal communication skills. ¿	Ability to communicate effectively with internal staff, managing agents, and other external stakeholders. ¿	Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced and evolving environment. ¿	Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. ¿	Ability to respond effectively to data requests and translate data into clear and meaningful information for stakeholders. ¿	Ability to work across multiple teams and provide analytical and operational support based on organizational priorities. ¿	Ability to learn and navigate multiple databases, systems, and business processes. ¿	Knowledge of affordable housing programs, homeless housing programs, and housing subsidies, including relevant New York City regulations and government programs. ¿	Ability to adapt to changing program requirements, business processes, and technology. Minimum qualifications: 1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and two years of experience in community work or community centered activities in an area related to the duties described above; or  2. High school graduation or equivalent and six years of experience in community work or community centered activities in an area related to the duties as described above; or  3. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. However, all candidates must have at least one year of experience as described in "1" above. Preferred skills:
