jobs.description: The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) is the City agency responsible for regulating for-hire transportation in New York City, including taxis, street hail liveries, high-volume for-hire services such as Uber and Lyft, black cars, luxury limousines, livery vehicles, commuter vans, and paratransit vehicles.  The TLC oversees a transportation ecosystem that moves nearly 1 million riders every single day the equivalent of the entire Boston transit system. TLC is the agency responsible for regulating New York City's taxicab and for-hire vehicle industry. With approximately 180,000 licensed drivers, 1,000 businesses, 115,000 vehicles including and the iconic yellow taxi at the heart of our city’s identity, TLC is entering a new era of dignity, accountability, and collaboration across the for hire vehicle sector. TLC continues to be on the front lines of a rapidly changing mobility landscape and our innovative efforts--whether requiring minimum pay for app drivers, ensuring wheelchair accessible service, making our licensed fleet more environmentally sustainable, working to eliminate traffic fatalities, or preventing discriminatory service--often serve as a model for other cities.  In this New Era for TLC, the agency is guided by three core priorities: - Driver and Passenger Dignity ensuring every interaction reflects respect and fairness - Corporate Accountability holding regulated entities to consistent, transparent standards - A Transportation System that Works Together equitable, modern, and accessible  The New York City Taxi & Limousine Commission (TLC) oversees a transportation ecosystem that moves nearly one million riders every single day, making it the third largest mode of transportation for New Yorkers. The TLC is responsible for regulating New York City's taxicab and for-hire vehicle industry. With 180,000 licensed drivers and the iconic yellow taxi at the heart of our City’s identity, TLC is entering a new era of worker dignity, accountability, and collaboration across the for hire vehicle sector. TLC continues to be on the front lines of a rapidly changing mobility landscape. Our innovative efforts--whether requiring minimum pay for app drivers, ensuring wheelchair accessible service, making our licensed fleet more environmentally sustainable, working to eliminate traffic fatalities, or preventing discriminatory service--often serve as a model for other cities.  The Deputy Commissioner for Policy and External Affairs will shape and amplify a new chapter of TLC, focused on three major strategic priorities: driver and passenger dignity, corporate accountability, and a transportation system that works together. This is a rare opportunity to lead on policy for one of the most visible, impactful, and culturally resonant public agencies in New York City.  Under the leadership of the Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice, the TLC is committed to improving the economic welfare of its 180,000 drivers. The TLC oversees a complex market of fleets, bases, ride-share apps, drivers, and passengers. We are seeking a Deputy Commissioner who is a policy visionary that can think strategically think about balancing competing marketing dynamics to ensure that the market fairly serves drivers and passengers. As one of largest regulators of ride-share platforms in the nation, a successful candidate will have expansive thinking that can enact a new era of transparency and fairness for our drivers.   The Deputy Commissioner will report to the Commissioner and will serve as TLC’s policy leader. The Deputy Commissioner will oversee the following teams: Policy Research, Data Analytics & Engineering, and Community Affairs.  As the person in this position will oversee a team carrying out technical analyses of large datasets, they need to be comfortable not only reviewing data but speaking about how it informs policy decisions to audiences with varying levels of technical understanding, ranging from technologists to elected officials and the press. A successful candidate will deeply understand the importance of engaging with drivers and integrating community engagement into a broader strategic vision.   Key Responsibilities •  Serve as TLC’s policy leader, working closely with the Commissioner, to set the strategic direction for the agency’s approach to labor, tech, and transit policy challenges •  Lead integration of economic justice into the TLC’s policy and program work, including workforce access, worker protections, and pathways to economic stability. •  Supervise policy, data, and outreach teams, ensuring strong alignment, accountability, and performance •  Direct intra-agency work-streams with legal, operations, enforcement, and financing teams to leverage the agency’s powers for policy implementation •  Conduct major policy studies and strategic reports that are driven by data insights   •  Coordinate closely with the communications team to strategically highlight policy work and the agency’s vision •  Lead coordination with City agencies to align policy and program efforts impacting TLC drivers •  Serve as the Commissioner’s top policy advisor, providing support on policy development, research and build a strategic policy vision for the agency.  •  Lead development of public reports and supporting the communications team to leverage media engagements •  Integrate the work of policy, data, and driver outreach into strategic plan that deeply embeds the voice of drivers in policy development  *Proposed salary will be determined based on experience and preferred skills of the selected candidate.”  To Apply: Please go to nyc.gov/jobs and search for Job ID# 802708 or click the "Apply" button below.  SUBMISSION OF A RESUME IS NOT A GUARANTEE THAT YOU WILL RECEIVE AN INTERVIEW.  APPOINTMENTS ARE SUBJECT TO OVERSIGHT APPROVAL.  Work Location: New York, NY Minimum qualifications: 1. A master's degree from an accredited college in economics, finance, accounting, business or public administration, human resources management, management science, operations research, organizational behavior, industrial psychology, statistics, personnel administration, labor relations, psychology, sociology, human resources development, political science, urban studies or a closely related field, and two years of satisfactory full-time professional experience in one or a combination of the following: working with the budget of a large public or private concern in budget administration, accounting, economic or financial administration, or fiscal or economic research; in management or methods analysis, operations research, organizational research or program evaluation; in personnel or public administration, recruitment, position classification, personnel relations, employee benefits, staff development, employment program planning/administration, labor market research, economic planning, social services program planning/evaluation, or fiscal management; or in a related area. 18 months of this experience must have been in an executive, managerial, administrative or supervisory capacity. Supervision must have included supervising staff performing professional work in the areas described above; or 2. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and four years of professional experience in the areas described in "1" above, including the 18 months of executive, managerial, administrative or supervisory experience, as described in "1" above. Preferred skills: - At least 8 years of experience in policy development, public affairs, government, advocacy, or related fields.  - A graduate degree in public policy, urban planning, economics, or another relevant field. - Experience managing a team with diverse portfolios and fostering professional development and engagement. - Excellent written and verbal communication and problem-solving skills. - Exceptional political acumen and the ability to navigate complex environments with grace and clarity. - Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment, including responding to emerging issues. - Proven expertise in developing, implementing, and being accountable for complex strategies, supported by strong qualitative and quantitative data analysis skills. - Commitment to equity, dignity, accountability, and excellence in public service.  The strongest candidates will also demonstrate many of the following:  - Experience overseeing programs and/or policy portfolios at scale, preferably within government or a large public or nonprofit system. - A collaborative approach to working across teams and building relationships with senior leadership, colleagues, external partners, and stakeholders, including civil society, community organizations, think tanks, and academic institutions. - Experience developing and implementing impact-driven policy research and advocacy projects, including a track record of publications. - Experience working with diverse communities, ideally including immigrant, multilingual, and worker-centered populations. - Proficiency with statistical analysis and digital tools. - Proficiency in languages other than English is a plus.

The TLC oversees a transportation ecosystem that moves nearly 1 million riders every single day the equivalent of the entire Boston transit system. TLC is the agency responsible for regulating New York City's taxicab and for-hire vehicle industry. With approximately 180,000 licensed drivers, 1,000 businesses, 115,000 vehicles including and the iconic yellow taxi at the heart of our city’s identity, TLC is entering a new era of dignity, accountability, and collaboration across the for hire vehicle sector. In this New Era for TLC, the agency is guided by three core priorities: - Driver and Passenger Dignity ensuring every interaction reflects respect and fairness - Corporate Accountability holding regulated entities to consistent, transparent standards - A Transportation System that Works Together equitable, modern, and accessible  About the Role According to the TLC Driver Feedback Survey, 40% of drivers do not believe they are treated fairly by app companies, bases, or fleets. As the regulator of the largest taxi and for-hire transportation system in the United States, the TLC is strengthening oversight of the businesses that impact drivers’ ability to work, monitoring economic stability, and promoting a fair and sustainable transportation system that recognizes drivers’ essential role in keeping New York City moving.  The TLC is seeking an Industry and Market Analyst to join the newly-created Industry Accountability unit to research and analyze industry and market trends across the taxi and for-hire vehicle sectors. In addition, the new unit will conduct investigations and analyze trends in driver complaints to identify emerging issues and areas where TLC should focus its regulatory, enforcement, and policy efforts to strengthen worker protections and promote driver dignity. Reporting to the Executive Director, the analyst will develop and study economic models and forecasts to inform market and business conditions for taxis as well as app-based and traditional car services. The position will require engaging directly with drivers, fleet operators, and other industry-related businesses to gather quantitative and qualitative data to inform analysis. Candidates with experience in economics, finance, and/or commercial banking oversight, are strongly encouraged to apply. If you are interested in utilizing economic data to improve working conditions and business oversight, this may be a role for you.  Duties and Responsibilities - Support the Executive Director in analyzing market conditions, regulatory compliance, oversight structures, investigations, industry data, and policy impacts. - Develop and design audits, market analysis, and investigations of industry practices across taxi, high-volume for-hire companies (Uber and Lyft), traditional car services, and other TLC regulated businesses to identify practices that may adversely affect drivers’ earnings, working conditions, access to trips, or ability to participate fairly in the industry. - Create and maintain financial models and forecasts for TLC-regulated industries to inform market conditions, identify trends, or changes that warrant further review or intervention. - Translate economic and analytical findings into easy to understand memoranda, reports, and presentations for senior leadership. - Consult and partner with internal cross-functional teams and external industry experts to achieve unit objectives and goals. - Complete special assignments, tasks, and projects assigned by senior management as needed. Preferred skills: The successful candidate should possess the following: •	Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) operating system administration and support experience •	OpenShift container platform administration and operational support experience •	Ansible automation platform development, maintenance, and orchestration experience •	Build standards, hardening, and compliance validation experience

jobs.description: About the role: The Research Analyst for the Advancing Universal Representation (UREP) Initiative works in a supporting research role to build and share evidence in support of the Initiative’s goal to advance policies and programs that support due process in the immigration system by: 1) expanding access to legal representation for immigrants facing deportation—with the ultimate goal to establish a federal right to government-funded counsel for all immigrants facing deportation who cannot afford an attorney—and 2) combatting the harms of immigration detention. The Research Analyst collects, manages, and analyzes primarily quantitative and occasionally qualitative data; assists in the writing of reports and other research materials to support the Initiative’s strategic advocacy and policy priorities; fields rapid response research requests; conducts literature reviews; supports the generation and design of new research; reviews documents; and presents findings from research projects. In this role, the Research Analyst reports directly to the Principal Research Associate, with support and mentorship from the Research Associate, the Principal Data Scientist, and the Associate Director of Research for the UREP Initiative and will also develop and strengthen their own skills and work independently. The Research Analyst contributes to and supports discrete tasks but also has some task ownership and task management. The Research Analyst primarily works on qualitative research projects, which requires independent coding and analysis, and will also occasionally perform tasks beyond research-specific tasks, including some advocacy and administrative work. The Research Analyst collaborates with team members to advance Initiative goals by actively engaging in team meetings and program activities. The Research Analyst is also expected to support efforts to ensure Vera’s Race, Equity, and Inclusion priorities are a core aspect of Vera’s mission, both internally in how team members work together, and in research, including in methodological approaches, publications, hiring and staffing, and external and internal research communications. 1. Data collection, management, and analysis Clean and manage data (primarily quantitative). Develop and maintain code, codebooks, instruments, or other research materials. Support data collection under the supervision of senior research staff. Support quantitative and qualitative analysis of data and/or write up of methods and results. 2. Rapid Response Field rapid response data requests from team members and external partners, including quickly producing programmatic and immigration court statistics, identifying and sharing existing research to provide evidence in support of advocacy materials, and more. 3. Write up / presentation of research Prepare and format reports, factsheets, and other products. Conduct background research and compile materials, including literature reviews. Prepare data, statistics, background research, or data visualizations for reports and other products. 4. Team Support and Internal Collaboration Carry out special projects in support of the Initiative’s research agenda or another program under the supervision of senior research staff. Support other lines of work within the Initiative (i.e., advocacy, programs, and blueprint design) on a variety of assignments, as needed. Contribute to research project development and design. Participate in cross-cutting Initiative events and lobbying activities, as needed. 5. Administrative Tasks Manage and respond to emails from external partners who work with Vera. Schedule and facilitate meetings. Data entry tasks, including creating, updating, and maintaining spreadsheets and databases. What qualifications are we looking for? Required : Bachelor’s degree in statistics, computer science, or social science, or related field + up to 3 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a Bachelor’s degree, applicable work or life experience may be considered. Preferred : A demonstrated interest in research, and/or some experience using research methods in academic or applied settings. Experience with the immigration legal system and/or immigration policy through lived or work experience. Lived experience as a person directly impacted by the criminal-legal and/or immigrations system A demonstrated commitment to racial justice Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities you'll bring: Experience in quantitative research (e.g. completing a research project using quantitative methods). Coding experience, preferably for data analysis, in Python (highly preferred) R, Stata, or SQL. Ability to synthesize complex literature and share findings from existing research. Skilled in writing findings from research in a manner that is easily understood by the general public. Careful attention to detail. Developing ability with data visualization and presentation and a desire to learn more. Spanish language proficiency a plus. Location: Please note this role will report to our Brooklyn, NY office. Vera employees adhere to a hybrid schedule and are in-office on an alternating schedule that generally amounts to 10 days per month. Compensation and Benefits: The compensation range for this position is $64,000 - $67,000 . I n addition, this position is part of a bargaining unit represented by the Association of Legal Aid Attorneys (ALAA) UAW 2325 . Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience and performance. The salary range listed is just one component of Vera Institute’s total compensation package for employees. As an employer of choice in our field, supporting Vera staff - both personally and professionally - is a priority. To do this, we invest in the well-being of our staff through other rewards including merit pay, generous paid time off, a comprehensive health insurance plan, student loan repayment benefits, professional development training opportunities and up to $2,000 annual for education costs and fees relevant to Vera work, employer-funded retirement plan, and flexible time. To learn more about Vera’s benefits offerings, click here . Application Process: To receive further consideration for this career opportunity, applicants are asked preliminary questions about logistics, their interest and qualifications. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional details about their experience via a phone screen/form in advance of an invitation for a virtual or in-person interview with the team. Some searches may explore scenarios during the interview process and/or an assessment prior to reference checks and a hiring decision. Applications may also be faxed to: ATTN: People, Place, and Culture / [JOBTITLE] Vera Institute of Justice 34 35th St, Suite 4-2A, Brooklyn, NY 11232 Fax: (212) 941-9407 Please use only one method (online, mail or fax) of submission. No phone calls, please. Only applicants selected for interviews will be contacted. Vera is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without unlawful discrimination based on race, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, military status, prior record of arrest or conviction, citizenship status, current employment status, or caregiver status. Vera works to advance justice, particularly racial justice, in an increasingly multicultural country and globally connected world. We value diverse experiences, including with regard to educational background and justice system contact, and depend on a diverse staff to carry out our mission. For more information about Vera, please visit www.vera.org .
